title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) using the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter and shared controlled-fault candidates, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation was invalid and excluded per the preregistered rule). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11=29, n10=9 (guarded-only), n01=1 (baseline-only), n00=0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.2051282051 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.0769230769, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Execution used the declared model gpt-5-mini and recorded 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120). We report preregistration adherence, exact execution accounting, statistical inference, limitations (synthetic faults, single model, simulator-backed success predicate), and archival pointers for reproducibility.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to assist network operations by producing device configurations and remediation plans. A common safety pattern is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that interposes a deterministic verifier (or simulator) between probabilistic generation and acceptance. Prior work in code, Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC), and related DSLs reports that verifier-interposed repair can raise verifier-detected pass rates and provide diagnostics useful for automated repair [1], [2]. However, controlled evidence specifically targeting vendor CLIs (e.g., Cisco/Juniper) with preregistered fault operators and paired causal estimands is limited. We therefore ask: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults? Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment design and frozen task bank; (2) a completed confirmatory execution under hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 using shared controlled-fault candidates and the declared model gpt-5-mini; (3) a paired analysis reporting a +20.51 percentage-point absolute increase in verifier+simulator pass rate for guarded versus baseline (p=0.021484375; 95% CI [0.0769230769,0.358974358974359]); and (4) an archived artifact bundle containing raw outputs, verifier traces, execution manifest, and analysis artifacts.
sections.related_work: Empirical GVR demonstrations in code and IaC indicate that deterministic verifiers interposed in generation–repair pipelines can materially increase verifier pass rates and supply actionable diagnostics for repair [1], [2]. Controlled analyses highlight a class of risks where iterative refinement optimised against a single proxy verifier can produce degraded true-target behaviour (verifier-exploitation) and emphasize the need to instrument verifier-mediated pipelines for both efficacy and failure modes [3]. Complementary investigations document a measurable verifier "tax" (increased interaction horizon, compute/cost) that affects operational feasibility [4]. These prior results motivate a controlled, fault-injection evaluation on vendor CLI templates to measure post-repair residual invalidity and to quantify harmful-edit incidence under a paired causal estimand.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand: The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (the paired difference in the verifier+simulator pass indicator). Design and adapter semantics: confirmatory execution used adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 with shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: for each task index a single deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate was generated and shared unchanged across both conditions. Each pair received exactly one initial generation (shared) and exactly one repair opportunity per condition; baseline denotes blind repair (no verifier diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. Note: the archived model_configuration records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Task bank and sampling: a deterministic fault injector produced 40 preregistered controlled-fault source candidates (manifest SHA-256 recorded). Confirmatory sample size and stopping: task_count fixed at 40; preregistered stopping required abort if the adapter contract could not be satisfied. Acceptance predicate and scoring: primary success required both the deterministic vendor-CLI verifier and a simulator-based compliance agreement to avoid verifier↔simulator discordance. Analysis: primary test was an exact paired binary test (two-sided McNemar exact or equivalent); we report discordant-pair counts, absolute risk difference, and a 95% CI computed via paired-bootstrap percentile (resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Missingness: the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule excludes a pair only if both condition executions fail for infrastructure reasons; one pair’s source generation was invalid/unscorable and excluded accordingly.
sections.results: Execution accounting: planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes = 78 (39 complete pairs); failed episodes = 2; hosted-model calls used = 118 (≤ planned maximum 120); source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). Primary outcomes (complete_pairs = 39): baseline success = 30/39 (0.7692307692307693); guarded success = 38/39 (0.9743589743589743). Paired contingency table (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Sensitivity and secondary analyses (per-fault-class summaries, harmful-change audits, contamination checks including verifier↔simulator discordance flags) are archived as exploratory artifacts and are not used to support the primary confirmatory claim in this paper. The single unscorable pair exclusion is documented in the execution manifest and analysis artifacts.
sections.discussion: Under the preregistered controlled-challenge and shared-candidate pairing semantics, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to the model substantially increased verifier+simulator-validated configuration success in our synthetic vendor-CLI task bank (approx. +20.5 pp). The shared-candidate paired design estimates the causal effect of diagnostic exposure on repair quality for the same injected fault candidate: both arms received the same controlled-fault candidate and identical repair budgets; only diagnostic exposure differed. Interpretational boundaries: (1) external validity is limited — confirmatory execution used synthetic controlled faults, a single declared model (gpt-5-mini), and one deterministic verifier+simulator; results do not by themselves establish production generality across vendors, models, or operator policies; (2) intervention activation was ensured by deterministic fault injection to make the intervention testable—naturalistic activation rates remain an open empirical question; (3) operational feasibility (the verifier tax: interaction length, model-call cost, and latency) was instrumented and archived but requires larger-scale cost/latency study before deployment claims; (4) verifier-exploitation risk persists for longer-horizon or multi-agent pipelines and requires mitigations (uncertainty quantification, calibrated abstention, multi-verifier schemes). All raw artifacts, verifier traces, provider call logs, and analysis files are archived to support independent verification and secondary analyses.
sections.conclusion:
In a preregistered, controlled-fault paired experiment using the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier-and-simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p=0.021484375; 95% CI [0.0769230769,0.358974358974359]). The evidence demonstrates that, under the controlled conditions and archived execution contract, deterministic verifier diagnostics can materially affect repair outcomes. Broader production claims require cross-vendor, multi-model, and operational cost/latency evaluations; the archived artifact bundle supports such follow-up work.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Adapter: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini). Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10) and cited here by immutable archive reference. Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: the archived model_configuration records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature=0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under the shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. Artifact availability: the execution manifest, raw_results.jsonl, provider traces, verifier traces, analysis artifacts, and hashes are archived in the evidence bundle. The run followed the preregistered stopping rule and adapter contract; no silent adapter substitution occurred.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and costs recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires further study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (uncertainty quantification, calibrated abstention, multi-verifier designs).
